questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a politician at a young age
The history of democracy in Ancient Greece
Good citizenship and a project for young people
Why paying taxes is important for everyone
questions.why: They discuss good citizenship and MyPolis, a project helping young people in Portugal re-engage.

questions.q: What does Georgie think makes a good citizen?
options: Someone who obeys the law and is kind
Someone who always votes in every election
Someone who works for the government
Someone who pays a lot of tax every year
questions.why: She says a good citizen doesn't break the law and is generally kind to other people.

questions.q: What does Neil add to Georgie's idea?
options: Good citizens should become local politicians
Good citizens should travel abroad more often
Good citizens should study their country's history
Volunteers, like people running kids' clubs
questions.why: Neil agrees and adds people who volunteer, like running clubs for children.

questions.q: What does Neil say about young people and politics today?
options: They vote more often than older people do
They vote less and often feel ignored
They trust politicians completely
They are all members of political parties
questions.why: He says young people are less likely to vote, and many aged 18 to 30 feel ignored by politicians.

options: Children vote in real national elections
Teachers decide how to spend school money
Children suggest changes; politicians respond
Politicians give long lessons about the law
questions.why: Children propose improvements and politicians listen, giving support or explaining why not.

questions.q: Why did Bernardo Goncalves start MyPolis?
options: He was worried trust in democracy was falling
He wanted to become a politician himself
His old school asked him to start it
He wanted to change the national curriculum
questions.why: He says there's been a quick erosion of trust, and a growing gap is 'very dangerous for democracy'.

questions.q: What benefit of MyPolis does reporter Alison Roberts mention?
options: It's completely free for all families
It only takes one day each school year
It is run entirely by older students
It can be part of the curriculum, not extra
questions.why: She says it's designed to be part of the national curriculum, rather than an add-on.

questions.q: Why is Myra Anubi especially impressed by the project?
options: Because children are paid to take part in it
Politicians, often hard to question, answer
Because it has spread to every country in Europe
Because the children fix everything themselves
questions.why: She's struck that politicians take the kids seriously, since politicians 'can be hard to pin down'.
